## Ctx.renderEditMedia() method

Edits an existing media message with dynamic type selection.

Template block: `<g-media>` (read via `getGMedia`<!-- -->).

**Signature:**

```typescript

IOptReplyVoice : T extends `video_note` ? IOptReplyVideoNote : T extends `sticker` ? IOptReplySticker : T extends `location` ? IOptReplyLocation : T extends `contact` ? IOptReplyContact : IOptEditMedia1) | null, options2?: IOptEditMedia2 | null, fallbackEdit?: IOptFallbackEdit): Promise<unknown>;
```

## Remarks

For media types that cannot be edited (voice, video\_note, sticker, location, contact), the original message is deleted and a new one is sent. Multi-src media groups cannot replace a single message, so supported pipe-delimited media groups also delete the original message and send a new media group.

If the edit itself fails, the fallback behavior is controlled by `fallbackEdit` (default `delete-reply`<!-- -->: deletes the original message and re-sends the same media — the result looks like an in-place edit). The fallback re-send drops `options1`<!-- -->/ `options2` (edit options do not map to reply options) and logs a `log.warn` when non-empty options are dropped; the re-send itself follows `Ctx.classifySendError` via `renderMedia` (`retryable` rethrows the original error untouched, `fallback-text` replies with fallback text). Fail-fast validation runs BEFORE any API call — programmer errors always throw, never fall back.

## Example


```typescript
async handleArgsCallback() {
  await this.renderEditMedia("photo")
}
```
